text:
Elena: quick follow-up from the RFC — proposing we pull metering/token-counting out of the request-router hot path into a dedicated 'metering' service. sketch below and questions.

Marco: curious — is the main goal latency on the router or better ownership for billing logic?

Elena: both. router is doing decode + routing + metering + quota check. metering spikes add jitter. also billing folks want clearer boundaries for audits.

Priya: sounds right. main risk is how we keep last-token correctness for quota enforcement. sync checks are easiest but add round trips.

Dave: from product side we need near-real-time counters for throttles and usage-based signals (within ~1s). eventual consistency beyond that is ok for invoices.

Elena: proposal: split into two APIs — Metering.sync_check(token_header) used for strict quota decisions (fast path, cached), and Metering.ingest(stream) for bulk accounting async. router calls sync_check only when a route is near limit. otherwise it emits an event to ingest.

Marco: that implies a small in-memory quota cache in router with TTL and leaky-bucket semantics. We need guardrails to avoid drift -> fallback to permissive when cache says allowed but metering disagrees.

Priya: fallback policy needs to be explicit. if metering unreachable, router should consult local cache and tag request with "metering-uncertain" for downstream accounting/ops. No silent failures.

Elena: Agreed. Also plan for cutover: Phase 1 — read-only split: router starts emitting ingest events, but still performs existing synchronous counts. Phase 2 — feature flag to enable sync_check for a subset of tenants. Phase 3 — widen and retire inline counting.

Marco: migration data model? We need idempotent ingest events and a commit log to replay counters in case of divergence. Suggest using append-only events to Kafka with dedupe by request-id.

Priya: operational concerns: observability (token-level latency, lost-event dashboards), backpressure behaviour when metering is overloaded. We should expose per-tenant circuit-breaker metrics.

Dave: billing/customer experience: what about invoices if we have short-term drift? Can we surface adjustments and a reconciliation window? Product OK with a 24–72h reconcile, needs clear docs.

Elena: yes — billing to publish reconciliation policy. For safety, we will keep sync path for enterprise tenants that opt-in for strict accounting during the transition.

Marco: security/attestation: metering becomes a sensitive surface. Add mTLS + signed event envelopes and an audit log. Also consider a read-only snapshot API for audits.

Priya: deploy plan: bake metering behind a new dedicated k8s service with horizontal autoscaling by partition key (tenant). Start canary with low-volume tenants, throttle ingest by rate-limiter.

Elena: sample header we'd add to events:

```
X-Req-Id: 3e7b9f
X-Tokens-Count: 78
X-Metering-Mode: async|sync
```

Marco: small UX ask — make the SDK add X-Req-Id so events are dedupable.

Dave: thumbs up from product. Also need public changelog entry and a migration doc for customers who rely on millisecond-accurate counters.

Priya: can we sketch SLOs? metering sync_check P50 < 3ms, P99 < 10ms; ingest 99.9% last-write within 5s. If we can meet that we can retire inline counting.

Elena: working draft of runbook and cutover steps incoming. tagging @Marco for API contract review and @Priya for ops checklist.

infra-bot: deploy requested: feature/metric-decoupling -> staging (ci-12345) :rocket:

Marco: I'll review API contract tonight. quick note — let's avoid name collisions: call the service "metering-bridge" for now (keeps term distinct from billing).

Elena: nice. I'll update RFC and add phased checklist + canary tenant list. thanks all :thumbsup:

Priya: will add circuit-breaker + dashboards to oncall runbook.

Dave: drop me a link when RFC updated, I'll prep comms for affected customers.

Elena: link: https://redwood-internal/rfcs/3961234567-metering-decoupling (draft).
